parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Show that the equation $\mathrm{f}(x)=0$ can be written as
$x = \sqrt{\frac{k}{2x+1}}$
where $k$ is a constant to be found.
(2)

parts.label: c

$x_{n+1} = \sqrt{\frac{k}{2x_n+1}}$
with $x_1=1$ and the value of $k$ found in part (b), find, to 4 decimal places,
(i) the value of $x_3$
(ii) the value of $\alpha$.
(3)

parts.mark_scheme:

dM1: Uses the double angle formulae $\sin 2\theta=K\sin\theta\cos\theta$ and $\cos 2\theta=\pm1\pm2\sin^2\theta$ to obtain $\sin 4\theta$ in terms of just $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$. If they use one of the other identities for $\cos 2\theta$, either $\pm2\cos^2\theta\pm1$ or $\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta$, they must subsequently change the $\cos^2\theta$ terms to $1-\sin^2\theta$

The functions f and g are defined by
$\mathrm{f}(x) = \ln(2x-3)$ $\quad x \in \mathbb{R}$ $\quad x>2$

(2)
parts.mark_scheme:

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$
(3)

parts.text:

(3)

parts.text:
The equation $|\mathrm{g}(x)|=10$ has two solutions.

(d) (i) find the value of $a$,
(ii) find the value of the smaller solution.
(4)

questions.stem:
The amount of an antibiotic, $x$ milligrams, in the bloodstream of a horse, $t$ hours after the antibiotic had been administered, is given by the formula
$x = D\mathrm{e}^{-0.2t}$
where $D$ milligrams is the dose of the antibiotic given to the horse.
A dose of 30 mg of the antibiotic is given to the horse.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the amount of the antibiotic in the bloodstream of the horse 8 hours after the dose is given. Give your answer in mg to 2 decimal places.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Substitutes $D=30$ and $t=8$ into $x=D\mathrm{e}^{-0.2t}$ and proceeds to a value for $x$
A1: AWRT 6.06. Allow this to be written down for both marks. Units are not important

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A second dose of 20 mg is given to the horse 8 hours after the first dose.
(b) Show that the amount of the antibiotic in the bloodstream of the horse, 2 hours after the second dose is given, is 17.5 mg to one decimal place.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: B1*: There are many ways to achieve this. Examples of correct expressions are $30\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times10}+20\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times2}$, $6.06\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times2}+20\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times2}$ (allow with more accurate values than 6.06), $26.06\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times2}$ (allow with more accurate values than 26.06). You need to see a correct expression followed by awrt 17.47 or 17.5 (units not important). Note that values other than 26.06 in $26.06\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times2}$ would still round to 17.5. For instance, expressions such as $26.1\times\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times2}$ and $26.07\times\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times2}$ would round to an appropriate value but will not score this mark.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
No more doses of the antibiotic are given. At time $T$ hours after the second dose is given, the amount of the antibiotic in the bloodstream is 10 mg.
(c) Find the value of $T$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
(Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.)
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:

A1: For a simplified equation in $\mathrm{e}^{-0.2T}$ (that is an equation that has a single $\mathrm{e}^{-0.2T}$ term). Look for $(3\mathrm{e}^{-1.6}+2)\mathrm{e}^{-0.2T}=1$ or awrt $26.06\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times T}=10$
dM1: Full method to find $T$. Condone slips but generally look for the candidate making $\mathrm{e}^{-0.2T}$ the subject, then taking lns, then proceeding to a value for $T$

- If they use their answer to part (a) it must be following an accurate answer to 2dp, e.g. awrt $26.06\mathrm{e}^{-0.2\times T}=10$
